name: Zurishaddai
title: Father of the tribal leader of Simeon
summary: Zurishaddai was the father of Shelumiel, who was the leader of the tribe of Simeon during the wilderness wanderings. He is mentioned in connection with the census and the offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle. His significance lies in his role as the ancestor of one of the tribal leaders of Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Census in the Wilderness
keyEvents.description: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, was appointed as the leader of the tribe of Simeon during the first census in the wilderness of Sinai.

keyEvents.title: Camp Arrangement
keyEvents.description: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, was given a specific place in the camp arrangement as the leader of the tribe of Simeon on the south side of the tabernacle.

keyEvents.title: Offerings at the Dedication of the Tabernacle
keyEvents.description: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, brought offerings on the fifth day during the dedication of the tabernacle, representing the tribe of Simeon.

keyEvents.title: Leader over Simeon's Army
keyEvents.description: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, was appointed as the leader over the military division of the tribe of Simeon when the Israelites broke camp from Sinai.
